gloss: to shudder; to tremble with fear; to be horrified

definitions.gloss: to shudder; to tremble with fear; to be horrified
definitions.explanation: To feel an intense chill or trembling from fear, horror, or shock at something terrifying or appalling.

examples.japanese: その{光景|こうけい}に{戦慄|せんりつ}した。
{犯行|はんこう}の{残忍|ざんにん}さに{戦慄|せんりつ}を{覚|おぼ}えた。
examples.english: I felt a shudder at the cruelty of the crime.

examples.japanese: {真相|しんそう}を{知|し}ったとき、{背筋|せすじ}が{凍|こお}るような{戦慄|せんりつ}が{走|はし}った。
examples.english: When I learned the truth, a spine-chilling shudder ran through me.

notes:
Composed of {戦慄|せんりつ} (shuddering; horror) + する. A literary, dramatic word frequently used in horror fiction, news about shocking crimes, and dramatic storytelling. More intense than simply being scared — implies a physical reaction of trembling.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {戦慄|せんりつ}を{覚|おぼ}える: to feel a shudder of horror
- {戦慄|せんりつ}が{走|はし}る: a shudder runs through (someone)
- {戦慄|せんりつ}すべき: horrifying; shudder-inducing
- {戦慄|せんりつ}の{事実|じじつ}: a horrifying fact

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {震|ふる}える: to tremble; to shiver — the basic word for physical trembling from cold, fear, or excitement
- {恐怖|きょうふ}する: to fear; to be frightened — focuses on the emotion of fear rather than the physical trembling
- ぞっとする: to shudder; to get the creeps — more colloquial; used for a momentary chill of fear or disgust
